sections.h2: Who sends a LaRue County property tax bill, and who answers questions about it?
sections.html:
LaRue County property owners deal with offices that all sit on or near West High Street in Hodgenville. The sheriff collects the current bill, the PVA sets the value, the county clerk receives bills that go unpaid, and the county attorney handles collection of delinquent ones. Hodgenville homeowners also get a separate city bill from City Hall.

  • Sheriff's Office. 209 West High Street, Suite 6, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; phone (270) 358-3120.
  • Property valuation administrator. Handles value, exemptions and appeal conferences; phone (270) 358-4202.
  • County clerk. 209 West High Street, Suite 3, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; phone (270) 358-3544.
  • County attorney. 209 West High Street, Suite 8; phone (270) 358-9223.
  • Hodgenville City Hall. 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.; phone (270) 358-3832 for city tax bills.

If a number on your bill looks wrong, call the PVA before you pay, because the sheriff only collects the amount the bill shows.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about LaRue County?
sections.html:
LaRue County is a rural central Kentucky county of 264 square miles, outside the Bluegrass region. Its seat and largest city, Hodgenville, had 3,235 residents in 2020 and is known as the birthplace of Abraham Lincoln. The county was established on March 4, 1843 from the southeast part of Hardin County and is part of the Elizabethtown-Fort Knox metropolitan area. Upton, which lies mostly in Hardin County, is the other city, and Buffalo and Magnolia are census-designated places. Hodgenville sits 12 miles southeast of Elizabethtown on Kentucky Route 61, and U.S. Route 31E runs through its center toward Bardstown and Glasgow.

The whole county is served by the LaRue County School District, whose campuses are in Hodgenville. The Lincoln Days celebration takes over downtown on the first full weekend of October. The county is also dry, which can matter to anyone selling a commercial building.

The Census Bureau estimated 15,184 residents in July 2025, up 2.1 percent from 2020. Its 2020 to 2024 QuickFacts show a stronger housing market than neighboring Appalachian counties:

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $183,500.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 79.4 percent across 5,996 households.
  • Median gross rent: $860.
  • Median household income: $67,067.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 59.

sections.h2: When are LaRue County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The county attorney's office states that bills are generally issued in October with a due date of December 31, and that payment goes through the sheriff from November 1 until April 15. For the 2026 tax year, county bills were mailed on October 30, 2026, and the Hodgenville city bills went out about the same time. The discount and penalty steps for 2026 bills are below.

Payment schedule for 2026 LaRue County bills (source: local newspaper notice of the sheriff and city schedule)
Paid betweenAmount owed
November 1 and 30, 2026Face amount less a 2% discount
December 1 and 31, 2026Face amount
January 1 and 31, 2027Face amount plus a 5% penalty
After February 1, 2027Face amount plus a 10% penalty, and a possible 11% sheriff's fee on county bills

Online payment by card carries a 2.5 percent convenience fee. A drop box inside the courthouse foyer takes payments at any hour, and mailed payments should include a copy of the bill and a stamped envelope if a receipt is wanted. The schedule changes each year, so look at the bill you receive before paying.

sections.h2: Is there a separate Hodgenville city tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes. A parcel inside Hodgenville receives a county bill from the sheriff and a city bill from City Hall, and each is paid to a different office. City payments are accepted at City Hall, through the city website, or in the city's drop box, and the 2% discount applies to payments made, mailed with a postmark or dropped by November 30.

A parcel outside the city limits gets only the county bill. When you buy or sell in Hodgenville, ask the closing agent to confirm both bills are paid or prorated. The sheriff's website lists a fire dues waiver form, and fire dues cannot be removed through the online payment portal, so a property owner who wants the waiver should file it with the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a LaRue County assessment?
sections.html:
The assessment date is January 1, and the real property tax roll opens for public inspection for thirteen days beginning the first Monday in May. Call the PVA at (270) 358-4202 and request a conference first; Kentucky requires that step before an appeal can be filed.

If the conference does not settle it, file the appeal with the county clerk by the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends. A local board of assessment appeals, made up of property owners, hears the case between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends. The board will deny an appeal that has no evidence behind it, so bring recent sales of similar homes, an appraisal, repair estimates or insurance values. The county attorney's page notes that its office assists the PVA in tax assessment appeals.

sections.h2: What happens if a LaRue County bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
If a bill is not paid by April 15, it is turned over to the county clerk and becomes a certificate of delinquency recorded as a lien on the real estate under KRS 134.122. The bill is also a personal obligation of whoever owned the property on January 1 of that tax year. The certificate adds penalties and fees and carries interest at 12 percent per year under KRS 134.125, so the amount grows each month.

  • The county attorney sends two notices before any sale to a third party.
  • After 90 days, third-party purchasers may buy the certificate by paying the amount due, under KRS 134.452.
  • The first offering of certificates each year is typically a tax bill sale held in August.
  • Payment on an unsold certificate goes to the County Clerk's Office at 209 W. High Street, Suite 3.
  • If a third party has bought the certificate, you must pay that purchaser.

A certificate cannot be sold to a third party while the taxpayer has a payment agreement with the county attorney's office or the property is in foreclosure or bankruptcy litigation involving the county attorney. Payment plans are available through that office at (270) 358-9223 for certificates not yet sold.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in LaRue County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled under a public or private retirement system, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value of their home for the 2025 and 2026 tax periods, according to the Department of Revenue. The home must be the owner's own residence on January 1.

Apply to the LaRue County PVA at (270) 358-4202 by December 31 of the tax year. Because the exemption reduces assessed value and not the bill itself, the savings depend on the combined county, school, city and district rates for your parcel. An owner who is selling a home is not required to file a new application before closing, but heirs who inherit a house should ask the PVA what changes once the title moves.

sections.h2: How are LaRue County taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
The person who owned the property on January 1 owes that year's bill, so a spring closing leaves the seller listed on the bill. The settlement statement usually splits the year between buyer and seller, and the closing agent pays the sheriff. The deed must carry an in-care-of address for the transfer-year bill under KRS 382.135(1)(d), so give the new owner's mailing address.

Before listing a LaRue County house with back taxes, get two figures. The sheriff can quote the current-year bill, and the county clerk can quote any delinquent certificate. If a house is inherited, behind on payments or in need of repairs that make a standard listing slow, a direct cash sale can pay off these amounts at one closing, provided the payoff is requested ahead of time.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in LaRue County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: County bills are paid to the LaRue County Sheriff's Office at 209 West High Street, Suite 6, in Hodgenville, by mail, in the courthouse drop box or online. City of Hodgenville bills are paid separately at City Hall, 200 S. Lincoln Blvd.

faqs.q: What is the discount deadline for LaRue County property tax?
faqs.a: For the 2026 bills, a 2% discount applied to payments made from November 1 through November 30, 2026. The face amount was due December 1 through 31, 2026. A 5% penalty applies for January 2027 and 10% after that.

faqs.q: What interest rate applies to delinquent LaRue County taxes?
faqs.a: After the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency on April 15, interest runs at 12 percent per year under KRS 134.125, along with penalties and fees. The county attorney's office can discuss payment plans for certificates that have not been sold.

faqs.q: How do I get the homestead exemption in LaRue County?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at (270) 358-4202 and apply by December 31. You must be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a retirement system, and own and live in the home on January 1. The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: Can I sell my LaRue County house if taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays with the property, so the payoff is settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the sheriff and the county clerk for written payoff figures before choosing a closing date.
